intro: The circus arrived overnight in a town that isn't on any map, its striped canvas rising between the clock tower and the river as though it had grown there. Admission is free, but the ticket-taker only lets you in if you can read your ticket, and half the crowd squints at the looping script as if it were a second language. Inside, the performers go about their business with a strange tidiness, each one sealing their act inside a small glass box and clipping a brass key to the lid. The ringmaster says nobody leaves until the boxes are opened, and the keys all hum like they know a tune. Between shows, the acrobats sit in a circle mending nets, humming fragments of songs that never quite finish, as if each voice were a word in a longer sentence spoken by someone else.
echo: The daring young man flew through the air with the greatest of ease.

puzzles.title: Strongman
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?

puzzles.title: Grand Finale
puzzles.flavor: Shaken, one word at a time.
hints: Each word is complete but shuffled. Start with the shortest ones: does a sentence appear?

puzzles.title: The Human Cannonball
puzzles.flavor: Fences and corners; some have an animal inside. Half a turn of the wheel and you'd have it.

partials.bd99b9a1a17541f59948aac141ba1462a2bbc177: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Picture the alphabet written into a couple of #-grids and X-grids. Which cell would each shape be? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: Hall Of Mirrors
puzzles.flavor: Everything that belongs is in there somewhere. Some things don't belong.

blocks.text: Somewhere in here: things to do with the big top.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.
The hidden words are: BARKER, FORTUNE, JESTER, LION, MIRROR, PRETZEL, SEAL, TENT, TICKET, TIGER, ZEBRA.

puzzles.title: Two Shows Daily
puzzles.flavor: Every letter here is wearing someone else's coat.

blocks.text: TDRDNW VJSVOPVN FTWDTV PD HVP PXQA GFY AD PXV SYQUV QA EZAP DTV MDYN XDDS

hints: Which short words are most common in English? Could any of them be hiding here?

puzzles.title: Midway
puzzles.flavor: A paint chart for a room nobody will ever decorate.
hints: Split each colour code into three pairs of hex digits. What else is a two-digit hex number?

meta.title: Meta: The Travelling Show
meta.flavor: The last lock takes every signature at once.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
